claims: Ichthyotitan severnensis means "giant fish lizard of the Severn".
Ichthyotitan severnensis is a newly identified species of giant Triassic ichthyosaur.
Ichthyotitan severnensis is estimated to be over 25 meters (>82 feet) long.
Paul de la Salle discovered a partial jawbone (surangular) in Somerset in 2016.
Paul de la Salle is a collector.
11-year-old Ruby Reynolds and her father Justin found a second, better-preserved jawbone chunk on Blue Anchor beach, Somerset, in 2020.
The 2020 jawbone discovery was reported by Earth.com.
Paleontologist Dr. Dean Lomax is from the University of Manchester.
Dr. Dean Lomax confirmed the pieces belonged to a new genus and species.
Dr. Dean Lomax worked with the finders to publish the research in PLOS ONE.
The fossils date back approximately 202 million years.
The fossils date to the end of the Triassic Period.
The finds include large pieces of the surangular.
The surangular is a bone in the lower jaw.
Analysis revealed unique internal bone textures common to giant ichthyosaurs.
